correctness.rationale: The proof reduces incident edges to codimension-one coarsenings using the published normal-fan face-poset theorem. The dimension formula forces exactly two coarsening mechanisms, each is classified explicitly, and the enumeration is reduced to marked right-to-left maxima with a reversible deletion/insertion bijection. A separate standard-library exhaustive checker directly reconstructs every codimension-one coarsening for \(n=2,\ldots,8\) and agrees with the closed formula in every case.
risks: The finite computation is not an infinite proof; correctness for arbitrary n rests on the written coarsening classification and counting bijection.

originality.rationale: The closest source gives a complete harmonic-triple face-poset encoding and only the qualitative statement that the fan is not simplicial. The new theorem extracts and proves an all-n local-degree formula, a sharp three-case classification of simple maximal cones, and a closed enumeration with asymptotic density. These are not stated as special cases or parameter substitutions in the inspected sources, and targeted published-index, web, and database searches found no matching statement. The face-poset theorem is an essential prior premise rather than a theorem whose displayed conclusion specializes to the new formula.
residual_risks: The complete face-poset description is very strong prior coverage; the originality here lies in the new local statistic and enumeration, not in new raw face data.
Terminology such as simplicial chambers or local normal-cone type could hide an uncatalogued equivalent statement.
risks: Because Proposition 2.4 determines the full face poset, the new theorem is a derived structural statistic of known combinatorial data; a reader could regard this as close to the source even though the formula, classification, and enumeration require additional arguments.

value.rationale: The harmonic polytope is explicitly known to be non-simple, and later expository work identifies non-simplicity as a practical disadvantage for its toric/Chow-ring use. The theorem quantifies that defect at the vertex level: it identifies exactly which vertices remain simple, gives their exact number, and shows their proportion vanishes. This is a natural structural statistic of the named polytope, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of a known table.
risks: The result is local combinatorics; it does not by itself resolve the geometric or algebraic difficulties caused by singularity.
